To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the overspread scattering function can be estimated with the same accuracy as its non-overspread counterpart, provided the overspread is not too large.

the overspread spreading function can be determined from a single measurement by a weighted pulse-train, that the overspread scattering function can be determined by averaging the overspread spreading functions, that the overspeed scattering function can be estimated by a novel estimator based on a weighted periodogram, and that the overspeed spreading function and the overspeed scattering functions are the only functions that can be determined in this manner.

the scattering function of a target can be estimated with a mean square error of order 1/N with N samples of a weighted pulse train, if the support set of this scattering function is compact and has finite Lebesgue measure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel channel sounding procedures and the analysis of the corresponding estimators.
the development of a novel estimator for scattering functions.
the estimation of the scattering function of a target from its echo response to a single weighted pulse train.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our estimator is a natural generalization of the periodogram estimator for arbitrary non-rectangular support sets.

we can determine the scattering function of a random medium or a target from a single weighted pulse train echo if the support set of its scattering function is compact and its second order moment is integrable.
we are able to estimate the scattering function in the time-frequency plane with a resolution which is independent from its geometry and area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide an estimator which is asymptotically unbiased and has a variance that decays as fast as the periodogram estimator in the case of a rectangular geometry, and which is consistent for any support set.
we provide a new estimator for the scattering functions of random media that is robust against the presence of noise and that does not require the knowledge of the support set.
we are able to provide a non-asymptotic analysis for a novel channel sounding technique, and that this analysis applies to a large class of radar scenarios.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scattering function can be estimated with the same accuracy as in the case of rectangular support sets, provided that the support is sufficiently smooth.
the estimator is unbiased, has the lowest mean squared error among all estimators with finite energy, is consistent, and has an asymptotic distribution that can be explicitly determined.
we can estimate the scattering function from the echo of a weighted pulse train, without any knowledge of the geometry of its support.
